reviews.frank_statement: FRANK is better modeled as a heterogeneous loop-of-loops whose material recurrent paths need explicit recurrence budgets, continuation/exit reasons, state deltas and adaptive regulation.
reviews.counterhypothesis: FRANK's behavior can be represented adequately as event-driven orchestration and generic state machines without any explicit recurrent control representation in ClayCode.
reviews.falsifier: A current general-purpose ClayCode lowering can express and verify the relevant nested recurrence, budgets and exits entirely through existing checked grammar and IR, with no new structured-control representation and no loss of replay semantics.
independent_checks: Current-run local executable differential experiment: 2,000 randomized nested-loop cases, 0 mismatches against an independent AST interpreter; 4/4 negative cases rejected.
MLIR SCF primary documentation independently represents while/for loops with explicit continuation conditions and loop-carried values.
Kohli et al. arXiv:2604.07822 independently reports inference-time recurrence benefits plus overthinking failure under excessive recurrence.
Bae et al. arXiv:2507.10524 independently demonstrates adaptive recursion depth as a generic computation-allocation mechanism.
adversarial_checks: Current checked G9 grammar was compared against the G9 V3 source and lacks general while/for/break/return productions despite a cycle construct and an if use in the spec.
The experiment required mandatory finite budgets and explicit halt reasons; unbounded/invalid budget input was rejected.
No FRANK runtime execution was treated as established by the local proxy.
reviews.reason: The need for explicit recurrent control survives, but it is refined into a generic structured-control/loop-carried-state compiler/IR requirement rather than a FRANK-specific cognitive primitive or biological organ.
reviews.claycode_action: Add/test a generic bounded structured recurrence/control-flow IR and lowering path; do not add a FRANK-only loop primitive solely from the architecture analogy.

reviews.frank_statement: Spectral-radius proxies, attractor classes, overthinking/stagnation indices and cross-loop coupling should become part of FRANK loop-dynamics observability.
reviews.counterhypothesis: These diagnostics may be useful only for specific numerical recurrent models and may not predict useful behavior in heterogeneous event-driven FRANK loops.
reviews.falsifier: On frozen H1 replay episodes, the proposed readouts fail to predict or discriminate useful convergence, productive cycles, stalls and unstable overthinking better than simpler residual-error/cost baselines, or interventions based on them do not improve outcomes.
independent_checks: Parcae primary project/paper evidence links recurrent stability to constrained recurrent dynamics in looped language models.
Blayney et al. arXiv:2604.11791 reports cyclic fixed-point behavior in looped reasoning models.
Current-run compiler experiment proves only representability of loop state/budgets/exits, not predictive validity of spectral or attractor diagnostics.
adversarial_checks: Bounded periodic behavior was explicitly kept separate from divergence in the newer FRANK note.
No scalar dynamics metric was allowed to become truth, emergence or effect authority.
No H1/FRANK runtime trace was available in this run to validate predictive utility.
reviews.reason: ClayCode can represent these metrics as typed observations, but their causal usefulness for FRANK remains unvalidated until H1 replay/intervention evidence exists.
reviews.claycode_action: Represent metrics as ordinary typed data/receipts, not privileged language semantics; defer controller-specific promotion.
